paragraphs: Imagine you discover a potion that makes you immortal. Drinking it would freeze your body at its current age, protect you from disease, and ensure survival for as long as the universe exists. The main question is: would you drink it?

Some philosophers see immortality as full of exciting possibilities. You could explore endlessly, pursue long-term goals, and never fear death. John Martin Fischer argues that certain pleasures, like watching sunsets, would stay enjoyable, and personal or social ambitions could always provide meaning. Others believe immortality has serious problems. Bernard Williams warns that life would eventually become unbearably monotonous, with repeated activities losing their charm. He also argues that constant change in values and identity could make life unstable, even meaningless. Samuel Scheffler adds that time limits are what make human life valuable: knowing we will die pushes us to make choices. For many, eternal life might be more of a curse than a blessing.

paragraphs: If you find a potion that gives you eternal life, would you drink it? The potion keeps you young, safe from disease, and alive forever.

Some philosophers say immortality brings freedom. You could travel, try new hobbies, and reach many goals without worrying about time. John Martin Fischer says some things, like sunsets, never get old. But other philosophers warn of problems. Bernard Williams says life would turn boring after repeating the same activities for centuries. Changing your habits and identity again and again could also feel confusing.
Samuel Scheffler adds that limited time gives life meaning, because we must decide what is important before we die. Eternal life, therefore, could feel like both a gift and a problem.

paragraphs: You find a magic potion. If you drink it, you will live forever. You cannot get sick, and your body will stay the same age.

Some people think that this is very good. You can do many things, travel, and still learn something new. You never need to be afraid of death. But some people think that it is not good. Bernard Williams says that life can get boring if you repeat the same things for many years. Samuel Scheffler says that life is special because it is short. When we know that time is not forever, we choose what is important. With no end, life may lose meaning. Living forever can be both happy and sad.
